Subject: DPA redline and deployment-mode appendix (Dedicated vs Private)

Hi Elaine —

Thanks again for the conversation this morning. Attached are: 1) our DPA redline (Novapay_DPA_redline_v3.pdf), 2) the current subprocessor matrix (subprocessor_matrix_2027-03-15.csv), and 3) a short deployment-mode appendix that clarifies how data flows and subprocessors differ between Dedicated (Redwood-managed GPU fleet) and Private/VPC (customer-controlled network or on-prem).

Quick notes on the appendix where Novapay asked for clearer language:
- Dedicated: data ingress exits Novapay's network to Redwood-managed hosts; we list the compute, storage, and telemetry subprocessors and the limited telemetry retained for operational debugging.
- Private/VPC/on-prem: data stays within customer network boundaries; Redwood's control plane only carries metadata for provisioning (no customer payload stored).
- Cross-border transfers: if Dedicated capacity is provisioned in a different region, we default to the contractual transfer mechanisms (SCCs + DPA clauses) unless you require region-locking.

Please review the redline and highlight any items you want us to change; the DocuSign envelope will be ready once legal confirms final language. If helpful, Laura (privacy) and Naomi (product ops) are copied for technical caveats.

Attachments: Novapay_DPA_redline_v3.pdf (pdf, 139KB), subprocessor_matrix_2027-03-15.csv (csv, 47KB), deployment-mode-appendix.docx (docx, 28KB)

Thanks,

Hi Karthik —

Thanks for sending these over. A few quick clarifying questions before we loop legal into redlines:
1) For Dedicated, can you confirm whether any model telemetry (prompt hashes, timing) is ever written to long-term storage outside of ephemeral logs? Our compliance folks want explicit guarantees.
2) For Private/VPC, the appendix says the control plane carries "metadata for provisioning" — can you list exactly what metadata fields are included? We need to put that in the DPA exhibit.
3) On subprocessors: I see a new analytics vendor in the matrix. Is that vendor used for usage-based billing or for product analytics? If the former, we need to map it to specific data categories.

If you can answer these by EOD Wednesday our legal team will do a redline pass.

Karthik —

Draft answers below that we can send to Elaine. I put suggested wording in brackets so legal can copy-paste into the DPA exhibit.

1) Telemetry retention (Dedicated): [Redwood only persists request metadata required for billing and operational debugging (request id, timestamp, model id, token count). We do not persist raw prompts or model outputs to long-term storage in Dedicated by default. Any longer-term retention for debugging is subject to customer opt-in and documented in the contract exhibit.]

2) Control-plane metadata (Private/VPC): [Fields include: customer org id, cluster provisioning id, API key fingerprint, node count, instance types, and region. No customer payload, prompts, or outputs are transferred to Redwood control plane for Private/VPC with on-prem configurations.]

3) Analytics vendor: The new vendor (PulseMetrics) is used purely for product usage metrics (anonymized counts) and billing reconciliation. It does not receive raw prompts or outputs — only aggregated usage counters and service telemetry. Add a line that billing uses aggregated token counts only.

If Naomi can confirm the PulseMetrics data flow, I will send a short email to Elaine with these points and attach a cleaned exhibit.

-Laura

Laura / Karthik —

Confirming PulseMetrics flow: we send them aggregated counters only (customer_id, model_id, daily_token_count, request_count). No prompt text, no outputs, no user identifiers beyond a hashed customer_id. We also pseudonymize request ids before shipping. SLAs require them to delete any aggregated daily buckets after 13 months per our policy — I'll note that in the exhibit.

I also added a one-line bullet clarifying that for Dedicated region locking can be requested during procurement and we'll reserve capacity in a single region. That avoids surprise cross-border storage.

I can produce a short exhibit (1 page) that includes exact metadata fields for Private/VPC. Ready to attach when you say go.

—Naomi

Hi Elaine —

Thanks for the questions. Per internal review, here are concise answers you can include in the DPA exhibit:

• Telemetry retention (Dedicated): Redwood persists request metadata required for billing and operational debugging (request id, timestamp, model id, token count). We do not persist raw prompts or model outputs to long-term storage in Dedicated unless explicitly agreed and documented.

• Control-plane metadata (Private/VPC/on-prem): customer_org_id, cluster_provision_id, api_key_fingerprint, node_count, instance_types, region. No payload (prompts/outputs) is transferred to the control plane for Private/VPC with on-prem configuration.

• PulseMetrics (subprocessor): receives only aggregated usage counters (customer_id hash, model_id, daily_token_count, request_count) and deletes aggregated buckets after 13 months. No raw prompts or outputs are shared.

We've attached a one-page exhibit that you can paste into your DPA draft; I've also indicated the procurement path to request Dedicated region-locking during capacity provisioning.

If that looks good to legal, I'll finalize the redline and send the DocuSign envelope. Are you comfortable with DocuSign or would you prefer AdobeSign?

Thanks,
Karthik
